Problem: How can a service that implements a command retrieve data from another service?
Context: You have applied the Microservices architecture pattern and the Database per service pattern. As a result, a service that implements a system command often needs to query other services. For example, the createOrder command implemented by the Order Service needs to retrieve the restaurants menu from the Restaurant Service to price and validate line items.
Solution: The solution consists of a Command service (the service that implements the command), a Provider service (the service that owns the data), and a Replica database (a read-only replica of the data from the provider service). The command service keeps the replica up to date by subscribing to Domain events published by the provider service.

Drawbacks: Simple components (makes command service more complicated)
Team autonomy (provider services team might need to coordinate more frequently)
Fast deployment pipeline (command services deployment pipeline might be slower)
Segregate by characteristics (potentially increased complexity if replica contains regulated data)
Simple interactions (provider services commands must publish events)
Efficient interactions (provider service might publish a large volume of events)
Minimize design-time coupling (risk of tight design-time coupling)

Related Patterns: Microservices architecture pattern, Database per Service pattern (creates the need), Saga (alternative solution), Domain event (generates the events), CQRS (structurally identical).
Uses: To allow a command-implementing service to retrieve data from another service without direct, potentially inefficient or tightly coupled, queries, by maintaining a local read-only replica.
